decisions.decision: One plan or a chain for B102 phases 2 and 3?
decisions.ruling: One plan finishes B102. The vwf callers move to bootstrap and tool-config is deleted in the same landing, so no released state has vwf calling a deleted skill.
decisions.rejected: A chain of two plans (phase 2, then phase 3)

decisions.decision: Does this plan also finish B103 (git-workflow merge model)?
decisions.ruling: Yes. B103 is in this plan.
decisions.rejected: A separate plan for B103

decisions.decision: Where does git-workflow read the merge model?
decisions.ruling: git-workflow reads merge_model of [branch.<destination>] from the .config/bootstrap.toml of each repository it lands in, the root and each member. When the file or the key is missing, the value is direct, bootstrap's own default. The MERGE_MODEL_DEVELOP, MERGE_MODEL_MAIN and legacy MERGE_MODEL env reads are deleted.
decisions.rejected: The env variables as a fallback; stop the landing and point to adopt

decisions.decision: How does init hand the repo shape to bootstrap?
decisions.ruling: init runs bootstrap's readme prompt, quoted word for word in init's SKILL.md and attributed to bootstrap's README.md. The same prompt also brings an adopted repository up to date, so /vwf:setup reshape reaches it through init. init drafts no values block and asks none of the questions docs/sync/ asks.
decisions.rejected: A bootstrap: adopt instruction with values blocks drafted by init; reading the prompt from the clone's readme at run time

decisions.decision: Which of init's own passes stay?
decisions.ruling: init keeps the hygiene files (README, LICENSE, CONTRIBUTING; CONTRIBUTING rewritten to bootstrap terms), the enforcement.kept_files record in .config/vwf.yaml, and the forge pass (the backlog project; the PR rule expected from [branch.*].merge_model in .config/bootstrap.toml). It drops the secrets-provider pass, the git landing question, the trust check, the mise run init step and the _default slots. init/references/tool-configs.md is deleted.
decisions.rejected: Keep the secrets pass (two owners of secrets setup); drop the forge pass too

decisions.decision: What do shaped and drift mean after tool-config?
decisions.ruling: Shaped means the repository has .config/bootstrap.toml. Drift means mise run setup:configs --dry-run shows a change (bootstrap docs/sync/index.md, the done-check of step 6). A repository with .config/stackgen.yaml and no .config/bootstrap.toml is old layout: setup Step 0 offers init. A .config/stackgen.yaml beside a .config/bootstrap.toml is a doctor Leftovers row. init deletes .config/stackgen.yaml after a green adoption. The doctor checks of stackgen.yaml members, repo_name and the mise layout (miserc, conf.d _base/ and ai/) are deleted; the PR-rule check reads [branch.*].merge_model.
decisions.rejected: Shaped by bootstrap.toml with no drift check

decisions.decision: Does config_format change?
decisions.ruling: No. .config/vwf.yaml keeps its keys and kept_files stays. setup Step 0's old-layout detection is the migration path; bootstrap's docs/sync/migrate.md maps the old keys.
decisions.rejected: A config_format bump to 26 with a migrate step

decisions.decision: What happens to setup's materialize pass?
decisions.ruling: It loses every tool-config call: pack, pack-remove, preview and the re-derived all call. The pack values: text is deleted (the values: key was removed in phase 1, bc95a7af). setup reads nothing from .config/stackgen.yaml. The stackgen materializer, which already hands tools to bootstrap, is the one thing the pass calls.
decisions.rejected: none — follows from D1 and phase 1

decisions.decision: What happens to checker rule 15 and the tool-config code in check.ts?
decisions.ruling: Rule 15 (one formatter exclusion set) is retired, with its tests. Rules 16 and 17 keep their numbers; the docs say sixteen rules, rule 15 retired. The render.mjs import and SUBTASK_DIRS, the TOOL_CONFIG_* constants, toolConfigTrees() and every walk over the tool-config trees, and templateNameFaults are removed. Rule 11's allowlist under .config/ (test/, p/_project/) becomes a constant local to check.ts.
decisions.rejected: Retire and renumber 16 to 15 and 17 to 16

decisions.decision: Who removes the excludes that name the tool-config tree?
decisions.ruling: The plan edits no exclude. Root dprint.jsonc, .config/pre-commit-config.yaml and .config/linter.yaml are managed by bootstrap.
decisions.rejected: The gates unit edits dprint.jsonc; the plan edits all three

decisions.decision: Does the plan need a review unit?
decisions.ruling: Yes. U5 changes scripts/src/check.ts, which is tooling source that executes. One review unit covers U1 to U5.
decisions.rejected: The wave review alone

decisions.decision: Which plan runs first: this one or 2026-11-02-optional-tools-in-vwf-tools?
decisions.ruling: optional-tools runs first. This plan requires it and edits the files it left (setup, doctor, vwf-config.md, check.ts, the docs) in their post-optional-tools state.
decisions.rejected: This plan first, with optional-tools re-planned

decisions.decision: Which standing decisions are reversed?
decisions.ruling: Confirmed by the user: 2026-09-26-tool-config, 2026-09-26-tool-config-gates, 2026-09-27-tool-config-hygiene, 2026-10-05-shaped-means-stackgen-yaml, 2026-10-05-doctor-drift-by-preview, 2026-10-05-stackgen-yaml-replaces-vwf-answers, 2026-10-01-trust-is-the-users-setup-all-is-tool-configs, 2026-10-01-tool-config-renders-with-a-node-script, 2026-10-05-tool-config-templates, checker rule 15, and git-workflow's MERGE_MODEL_* env reads (the record 2026-09-20-branch-model). Also confirmed, reversed by D14, D24, D37 and D43: 2026-09-06-init-owns-the-first-commit, 2026-09-10-init-replaces-a-diverged-helper-library, 2026-09-12-init-brownfield-sidecar-and-diverged-files and 2026-09-20-init-brownfield-reads. The docs unit writes one new decision record and marks each reversed record superseded.
decisions.rejected: none

decisions.decision: Which of init's other sections stay, given that bootstrap makes the first commit, creates develop and asks before a push?
decisions.ruling: init keeps the sections that write its own files: §1 (the repository itself, git init before bootstrap), §4 placeholders, §5 template fallback, §7 renamed The project ids (the ids its own files use; the rest of §7 that fed the all call is deleted), §8 readme, licence and security file, §11(f) the forge pass, and §12 the report, rewritten without the rows of deleted steps. It deletes §2 the all call (replaced by the bootstrap step), §3 the secrets provider (D5), §6 hook fragments, §9 trust and mise run init, §10 the aggregator, §11(a) the landing model and §11(e) the push. §11(b) to (d) become one step: after bootstrap ends, hand the commits to /vwf:git-workflow with one consent (D37).
decisions.rejected: Keep init's git pass §11(b) to (e) as today

decisions.decision: What is a green adoption, and where does init delete .config/stackgen.yaml?
decisions.ruling: Green means the repository has .config/bootstrap.toml and mise run setup:configs --dry-run shows no change. init deletes .config/stackgen.yaml in each repository, base and each member, that is green, inside init's one consent; a repository that is not green keeps it, and the report names it.
decisions.rejected: Green means .config/bootstrap.toml exists, with no dry-run

decisions.decision: How is the result of mise run setup:configs --dry-run read, and what if the bootstrap clone fails?
decisions.ruling: By the exit code and the output. Exit 0 with no change listed means no drift; a listed change means drift; exit 5, or any other failure, means drift unknown. doctor reports unknown as a warning with the reason; setup Step 0 says it could not check drift and continues as current; init treats the repository as not green, keeps .config/stackgen.yaml and names the repository in the report.
decisions.rejected: A failed clone counts as drift

decisions.decision: Does doctor baseline, which recall runs at session start, run the networked dry-run?
decisions.ruling: Yes. baseline runs mise run setup:configs --dry-run in each repository. recall's text changes to match: baseline is no longer file reads only, and recall's not-shaped test is no .config/bootstrap.toml.
decisions.rejected: baseline stays file reads only, with the dry-run in doctor full mode and setup Step 0

decisions.decision: When is the consent to delete .config/stackgen.yaml asked, and which commit carries the deletion?
decisions.ruling: init's one plan, shown before the bootstrap step, lists delete .config/stackgen.yaml if the repository is green for each repository that has the file; the one consent covers it. The deletion rides init's own commit in that repository, base and each member, with init's own files; git-workflow makes that commit (D37).
decisions.rejected: A second question per repository after bootstrap ends

decisions.decision: Which lines of the setup:configs --dry-run output count as a change?
decisions.ruling: The dry-run prints its lines on stderr, each with the prefix repo-sync: (bootstrap's _scripts/repo-sync, _rs_log). Read stderr. After that prefix, a line that starts with would (would update, would remove, would chmod, would set bootstrap_commit) is a change. Lines that read unchanged, kept seed or skip are not. No would line and exit 0 means no drift. doctor, setup, init and recall all parse it this way.
decisions.rejected: none — follows from repo_sync's output format

decisions.decision: Does doctor baseline read the forge, and is the dry-run's cache refresh accepted?
decisions.ruling: baseline reads no forge, as doctor and recall say today; the forge check stays in doctor's full mode. The dry-run writes nothing in the repository; it refreshes bootstrap's own clone cache under ~/.cache/bootstrap, which D17 accepts.
decisions.rejected: none — follows from the standing baseline doctrine and D17

decisions.decision: setup:all is a tool-config task that bootstrap does not ship. What replaces it?
decisions.ruling: Every live mention of MISE_ENV=dev mise run setup:all becomes MISE_ENV=dev mise run setup, and a bare mise run setup:all becomes mise run setup; setup is the task bootstrap ships (setup/_default). The MISE_ENV=dev prefix stays where it is today, because bootstrap loads no conf.d file without MISE_ENV. History rows keep their text.
decisions.rejected: none — setup:all no longer exists

decisions.decision: What does git-workflow do with a merge_model value other than direct or pr, and is it a doctor finding?
decisions.ruling: git-workflow reads it as bootstrap's _scripts/merge does: pr means pr; any other value, or no value, means direct. doctor reports a value other than direct or pr as a warning with the remedy to fix .config/bootstrap.toml.
decisions.rejected: Stop the landing on an unknown value

decisions.decision: Bootstrap pushes its own commits, but init commits its own files after bootstrap ends. Who pushes init's commit, and which repo takes the forge pass?
decisions.ruling: init's one consent asks commit, or commit and push; git-workflow does the landing and the push (D37), members before the base, never a force-push. The forge pass runs once for the product, after the base lands, for each repo that git-workflow landed with a push this run (direct pushed the core branch, or pr opened the pull request), and for each repo that had nothing to land and whose core branches already exist on origin (the user's ruling); any other repo is pending on its Forge line with the reason.
decisions.rejected: init commits only and never pushes; the forge pass keyed on the remote state alone

decisions.decision: existing-repo.md surveys the repo against what tool-config lands (passes 1, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9, 10, the hook-manager row and the gate-configuration ordering). Which passes stay in init?
decisions.ruling: init keeps only the passes for its own files: pass 2 the readme and pass 6 missing files (the hygiene files and kept_files). It deletes passes 1, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9 and 10, the hook-manager row and The gate configuration commits first, alone: bootstrap's docs/sync owns them (migrate.md M3 task renames, M10 helper files). The passes left are renumbered, and every citation of an existing-repo pass, inside and outside init, names the pass by its title, never by its number.
decisions.rejected: Keep pass 1 as well; keep every pass and re-point passes 3 and 5 at bootstrap's migrate.md

decisions.decision: Nothing in bootstrap docs/sync reads .config/stackgen.yaml, so its merge_model, members and forge values are not carried over when init deletes the file. Does init carry them over?
decisions.ruling: No. Confirmed by the user: MERGE_MODEL_* is not used anymore; bootstrap uses a different approach. bootstrap docs/sync decides [branch.*].merge_model in .config/bootstrap.toml during adoption. init reads no value from .config/stackgen.yaml and carries none over; members stay in .config/vwf.yaml and the forge is read live.
decisions.rejected: init carries the merge_model values into .config/bootstrap.toml before the delete; init keeps the file when a value differs

decisions.decision: This repo's four release tasks (p/release, p/plugins/release, p/i/release, p/site/release) read the MERGE_MODEL and MERGE_MODEL_MAIN env, which no longer exists. Are they in scope?
decisions.ruling: Yes, confirmed by the user: they are repo-specific and migrate to .config/bootstrap.toml. Each reads merge_model of [branch.main] (the release branch) from .config/bootstrap.toml with yq, as bootstrap's _scripts/merge does: pr refuses the full sequence as today; any other value, a missing key or a missing file means direct. The MERGE_MODEL and MERGE_MODEL_MAIN reads are deleted. CLAUDE.md says the release tasks read [branch.main].merge_model in .config/bootstrap.toml. This reverses the standing rule that a plan never edits this repo's own .config files, for these four files only.
decisions.rejected: Park the env reads for a hand edit; describe the old env in CLAUDE.md; drop the sentence

decisions.decision: setup:ai:all, setup:ai:base and code:{format,lint,check}:all are tool-config task names that bootstrap does not ship. What do the docs say in their place?
decisions.ruling: The user ruled: setup:* and code:* are supported and owned by bootstrap. Each live mention of a tool-config task name becomes the bootstrap task that exists (setup:ai:all and setup:ai:base become setup:ai; code:format:all becomes code:format; code:lint:all becomes code:lint; code:check:all is dropped, since bootstrap ships no code:check). A passage names bootstrap as the owner of these tasks and does not restate what a bootstrap task does. History rows keep their text.
decisions.rejected: Rewrite each passage to describe the bootstrap task from its script

decisions.decision: What do git-workflow and the four release tasks do when .config/bootstrap.toml exists but yq cannot read it?
decisions.ruling: They stop, as bootstrap's _scripts/merge does, with the message cannot read the merge config of .config/bootstrap.toml. git-workflow offers no landing option; a release task exits 1 before it writes anything. A missing file still means direct.
decisions.rejected: Read a failed parse as direct

decisions.decision: setup Step 0 today counts the forge state (doctor's Forge state predicate) as part of current. Does it keep it?
decisions.ruling: Yes, confirmed by the user. Current means shaped, no bootstrap drift (D16, D19), and the Forge state predicate holds, read when the forge CLI is on PATH and logged in, else not checked. Only recall's line and doctor baseline stay local (D20).
decisions.rejected: Drop the forge read from Step 0 and leave it to doctor's full run

decisions.decision: U3 renumbers doctor's baseline predicates, and init and setup cite them by letter. How do citations stay correct?
decisions.ruling: Derived from D24. U3 keeps the bold title of each predicate it keeps: Pack versions, Project ids, Branches, Content drift (without its preview half) and Forge state, and titles the new dry-run check Bootstrap drift. Every citation of a doctor predicate outside the doctor skill names it by its title, never by its letter; U1 rewrites init/SKILL.md (817), existing-repo.md (489) and new-repo.md (888), U2 rewrites setup.
decisions.rejected: Fix the new letters in the plan before the run

decisions.decision: doctor's Project ids predicate compares commitScopes with the project ids, but bootstrap now owns commit_scopes. What does it do?
decisions.ruling: The user ruled: drop the commit-scope check. Project ids keeps its task-group check only; commit scopes are bootstrap's, and Bootstrap drift covers the synced config.
decisions.rejected: Read commit_scopes from .config/bootstrap.toml and warn on a missing project id

decisions.decision: D14 says init commits only what it wrote. Does the base commit still stage the gitlinks the member commits moved, and is a detached member still refused?
decisions.ruling: Yes, confirmed by the user. Members commit first; the base commit stages init's own files plus the gitlinks those member commits moved, and the report keeps the Gitlinks staged line. A member on a detached HEAD is still a refused row.
decisions.rejected: The base commit stages init's own files only

decisions.decision: Is shaped (has .config/bootstrap.toml) a titled baseline predicate?
decisions.ruling: No, as today: doctor reports not shaped on its own line, before the predicates, and evaluates no predicate in a repo that is not shaped. The titled predicates are those of D30. Derived from doctor's current shape.
decisions.rejected: Make shape a titled predicate

decisions.decision: init's hygiene assets and bootstrap's github tool both write .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/, and the forge value init read is gone. Does init keep the issue forms?
decisions.ruling: No, the user ruled: bootstrap's github tool owns the issue forms. init deletes its .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE assets and every row or sentence that lands them.
decisions.rejected: Keep them and write them when the origin host is github.com

decisions.decision: What does init do in a repo that has no .config/bootstrap.toml after the bootstrap step (the user stopped bootstrap's questions, or the clone failed)?
decisions.ruling: The user ruled: init stops in that repo. It writes no hygiene file, records no kept_files, makes no commit, no push and no forge pass there, and the report names the repo and the reason. The other repos continue. A stopped step can leave bootstrap's files uncommitted in that repo; the report then shows git status for it and says: commit or discard bootstrap's partial sync, then re-run /vwf:setup reshape (the user's ruling). init never cleans or commits a partial sync, and D38's clean-tree check stays strict. When the stopped repo is the base, the forge pass does not run (D23).
decisions.rejected: Continue with init's own files and skip only the push and the forge pass

decisions.decision: bootstrap docs/sync lets the user leave its sync uncommitted for review; pre-commit then refuses init's commit of its own files. What does init do?
decisions.ruling: The user ruled: bootstrap's sync is committed first. When the bootstrap step leaves changed or untracked files in a repo, init's one plan lists a first commit of those files in that repo, and the one consent covers it; init's own files go in a second commit. git-workflow makes both commits (D37). The first commit message names bootstrap's sync. Members commit before the base, as D32 says.
decisions.rejected: Write init's files and skip the commit; stop the repo as D35 does

decisions.decision: How does init land its commits, given bootstrap's no-commit-to-branch hook on main and develop, the merge models and the answer commit or commit and push?
decisions.ruling: The user ruled: init lands through vwf's git-workflow skill, not a landing engine of its own. In each repo, members before the base, init hands /vwf:git-workflow the commits to make, in order: the bootstrap-sync commit of D36 when there is one, then init's own files with the gitlinks of D32. git-workflow makes both commits itself, after it isolates the work (a commit on a protected core branch is refused by bootstrap's hook, so init cannot commit first), and owns branches, protected core branches, merge_model, conflicts, failures and reruns. init's one consent is the answer git-workflow needs: commit means commit only, with no push; commit and push means land and push. init has no push step of its own: §11(e) is deleted. A repo is pushed for the forge pass (D23) when git-workflow landed it with a push: direct pushed the core branch, or pr opened the pull request (the user's ruling). A repo git-workflow does not land is reported with its reason and is pending on its Forge line.
decisions.rejected: A vwf/init branch landed by init itself through code:merge:develop, code:merge:main or a local merge with SKIP (the earlier D37, D39 and D40, replaced because each added init-only landing cases)

decisions.decision: D36's sync commit is known only after the bootstrap step, but the one plan and consent come before it; and changed or untracked files can include the user's own earlier work. How is this handled?
decisions.ruling: The user ruled: before the bootstrap step, init checks every repo, the base and each member. If any tree is not clean, init stops the whole run before it writes anything and lists each dirty repo, because the one bootstrap prompt covers every repo and cannot skip one. The one plan carries a conditional line per repo: if bootstrap leaves its sync uncommitted, commit it first. On a clean start every change after the step is bootstrap's, so the one consent covers the sync commit.
decisions.rejected: Snapshot the dirty paths, exclude them, and ask a second consent after the step

decisions.decision: With the secrets provider gone (D5), init no longer calls the stackgen materializer, and deleting §2 of new-repo.md whole drops parts the kept passes need. What survives?
decisions.ruling: The user accepted: (1) init drops the materializer detection (SKILL.md 320–335) and its halt when none is installed; init calls no materializer. (2) Pass 6, missing files, runs over init's own hygiene assets only: the files init would write; a hygiene file the repo already has is kept, as today. (3) From §2, the hygiene-asset lay-down and the .config/vwf.yaml stub that holds kept_files survive, moved into the hygiene step; The answers each fetch carries and the materializer's Skipped and conflict rows are deleted, except the hygiene skips on init's own condition.
decisions.rejected: Keep a materializer dry-run so pass 6 also offers replace-or-keep over pack files

decisions.decision: init no longer writes the p/<slug>/_default slots. Who creates a project's task group, and do init's question 1 (repo name) and question 2 (project ids) stay?
decisions.ruling: The user ruled: a task group comes only from a pack's p/_project/ tasks, which setup's materialize pass renames to p/<id>/. doctor's Project ids checks only projects whose pinned pack ships p/_project/. init drops question 1 (repo_name is bootstrap's) and keeps question 2 only where its own files use the ids.
decisions.rejected: init writes an empty p/<slug>/_default for each project and keeps both questions

decisions.decision: init's §1 makes develop the first branch and §11(d), now deleted, created main. Bootstrap's docs/sync makes the first commit on main and handles the core branches. Who creates develop and main?
decisions.ruling: The user ruled: bootstrap. §1 runs a plain git init and nothing more. doctor's Branches remedy is bootstrap's docs/sync, reached through /vwf:setup reshape, whose bootstrap step runs it; it no longer says init creates the missing branch.
decisions.rejected: init keeps creating develop and main after bootstrap ends

decisions.decision: A repo with no commit holds only untracked files, so D38's clean-tree check fails it. Bootstrap's first commit holds only its two-line .gitignore. What does init do?
decisions.ruling: The user ruled: D38 applies as written. A repo with no commit and untracked files stops the whole run, and the report says: commit your files, then re-run /vwf:setup reshape. A repo with no commit and no files is clean and passes. The user's files never enter a bootstrap commit.
decisions.rejected: Record the untracked paths and leave them out of the sync commit; exempt a repo with no commit

decisions.decision: init runs no materializer and /vwf:setup reshape runs no materialize pass. What remedy do doctor's pack rows name?
decisions.ruling: The user ruled: rows about packs (Pack versions, the hash half of Content drift, a missing pack lockfile, Project ids) name /vwf:setup, a full run whose materialize pass re-pins and re-copies packs. Rows about bootstrap (Bootstrap drift, Branches, not shaped) and Forge state name /vwf:setup reshape. Every passage that says all rows share one remedy is rewritten: doctor's §9, the baseline mode and recall print one remedy line per remedy, each with the rows that led to it. A file in enforcement.kept_files is still skipped by every check, a pack file included (the user's ruling); only the sentences that say init or pass 6 records pack files are deleted (D41).
decisions.rejected: Give /vwf:setup reshape a materialize pass so one remedy covers every row

decisions.decision: G10: U6 security findings did not converge. Keep the bootstrap dry-run in doctor baseline and recall, return it to explicit runs, or require content-tied trust; and how to treat the unpinned bootstrap?
decisions.ruling: The user ruled: explicit runs and a handoff item. This reverses D17 and changes D20. (1) doctor baseline stays file reads only, and recall runs no mise task and no bootstrap code. The dry-run mise run setup:configs --dry-run runs only in doctor full mode and in setup Step 0. Recall and baseline say that they do not report config drift, and name doctor full mode as the place that does; recall keeps its not-shaped test of no .config/bootstrap.toml. D20 stays for the forge read; the refresh of the bootstrap clone cache now occurs only on these explicit runs. (2) This plan does not edit bootstrap. Doctor and setup state that an explicit dry-run executes the main branch of bootstrap with no pin, and that the trust gate of mise is not tied to file content. A request to bootstrap for a reviewed-commit pin is recorded as an open gap of this plan, for the user to hand to bootstrap. U6 reviews against this ruling: unpinned execution on an explicit run that discloses it is not a finding.
decisions.rejected: Keep the dry-run in baseline and recall; require content-tied trust, which mise does not supply
